clue.text: Original advantage involved in capturing king

indicators.note: capturing means the jumbled letters hold another piece inside them
involved suggests the letters of advantage are tangled up and rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: An original edge gained by taking the opponent's king, as in chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges ADVANTAGE into AVANTGADE, and 'capturing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde work is innovative and new, so original in the sense of pioneering.

clue.text: People are keen take part in such a society

definitions.text: People are keen take part in such a society

parts.words: People are keen take part in such a society
parts.note: a society whose keen members put on plays is an amateur theatrical club of this kind

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic club everyone wants to join.
explanation.walkthrough: Any club seems meant, but the society is one for amateur stage productions.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur theatre group is commonly called a dramatic society.

clue.text: Plot involved danger

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of danger are tangled up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A conspiracy that put people at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a scheme, but here it is a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land behind a house, planted with flowers or vegetables, is a synonym.

clue.text: Record appearance of full moon

definitions.meaning: a gramophone record is a flat round ... of vinyl
the full moon looks like a flat bright circle in the sky

explanation.surface: A log entry noting what the full moon looked like.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a vinyl record and the full moon seen from Earth are flat circular shapes.

clue.text: Tyrant captures northern retreat — it's hopeless

indicators.note: captures means the tyrant's word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a despot is an absolute ruler, a tyrant
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A tyrant seizes a northern hideout, and resistance seems futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone despondent has lost heart, feeling dejected and without any optimism.

clue.text: Girl following music group may be spotted

indicators.note: following means the girl's name comes after the music group

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl trailing a band might be noticed by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be spotted' looks like being seen; it means having a polka-dot pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large patterned neckerchief, classically printed with white spots.

clue.text: He is, or could be, a shopkeeper

indicators.note: could be means these letters may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Is he, or might he be, a shopkeeper?
explanation.definitionFit: A hosier is a retailer selling stockings and socks, a particular kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Guns raised, when animal being hunted appears

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gats is old slang for pistols or guns

explanation.surface: Hunters lift their guns when the quarry comes into view.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer hunting traditionally targets the male red deer as the quarry.

clue.text: It's a lever that may be turned to many uses

indicators.note: may be turned means these letters can be twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: A lever is a handy tool that can be put to all sorts of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptable to many uses has a wide range of applications and functions.

clue.text: Concerning a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: Something to do with a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions, both mean on the subject of or regarding.

clue.text: Kind of people who follow the herd

definitions.text: Kind of people who follow the herd

parts.words: Kind of people who follow the herd
parts.note: follow the herd usually means conformists; here people literally travel with their livestock

explanation.surface: Sheep-like conformists who copy everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom suggests conformity, but these people move with their grazing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering pastoral tribes migrate with their flocks and herds in search of pasture.

clue.text: Of course, it's sweet

parts.note: of course reads as naturally, but it means a course of a meal, the sweet one

explanation.surface: A cheerful agreement that something is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' seems to mean naturally; it is the dessert course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the sweet or dessert course is often called by this name.

clue.text: Board and fare

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to climb aboard it
to fare is to manage or progress, as in how are you faring

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to climb aboard a vehicle and to progress or manage.

clue.text: Study a French instrument

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
un is French for a
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine a French musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate definition: the clue, a puzzle to be worked out, is itself an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or puzzling problem is exactly what this clue presents to the solver.

clue.text: They make women's dresses stand out

definitions.text: They make women's dresses stand out

parts.words: They make women's dresses stand out
parts.note: stand out sounds like being noticeable, but means literally held out wide from the body

explanation.surface: Accessories that make an outfit eye-catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand out' suggests being conspicuous; these things physically spread skirts outward.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian hooped petticoats of stiff fabric held skirts out in a wide bell shape.

clue.text: Male representative takes me in to see the bosses

parts.note: man means a male person

indicators.note: takes, with in, means the representative holds another piece inside
in completes takes ... in, signalling one piece placed within another

parts.note: an agent is a representative acting for someone

explanation.surface: A man's agent brings someone along to meet the company heads.
explanation.definitionFit: The managers of a company, collectively, are its directing body.

clue.text: Further reflection about thinking of others

parts.note: re means about or concerning
consideration is thoughtfulness for other people

explanation.surface: Second thoughts on the subject of being kind to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking something over again is a further, second reflection on it.

clue.text: Fool's speech in production of Lear

definitions.text: Fool's speech in production of Lear

parts.words: Fool's speech in production of Lear
parts.note: suggests the Fool in King Lear, but also Edward Lear's output of comic verse

explanation.surface: The Fool's lines in a staging of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's tragedy comes to mind, but Edward Lear wrote famous comic verse of this sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish talk is gibberish, and Edward Lear's whimsical verse is the classic example.

clue.text: Took off

parts.note: took off can mean departed or removed, but also mimicked someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' suggests a plane departing; it means copied someone's mannerisms.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is British idiom for mimicking or impersonating them.

clue.text: Picnicking?

parts.note: a picnic is a meal taken outdoors, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually means dining at a restaurant; the question mark flags a literal outdoor meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a meal in the open air is literally taking food outside rather than at home.

clue.text: Entices casual worker with way to get a rise

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker

indicators.note: to get a rise in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Lures a temporary worker with a promise of a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or attract someone, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Looking, for example, to adopt a principle of Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: to adopt means to take something in, so the example holds the principle inside

parts.note: yin is the passive female principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Studying, for instance, the idea of taking up a Chinese philosophical principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something means watching or gazing at it closely.

clue.text: Cause anger by damaging a green

indicators.note: damaging suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ruining a village green or golf green would make people furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate someone is to make them furious.

clue.text: Remains within easy reach of Naples

definitions.text: Remains within easy reach of Naples

parts.words: Remains within easy reach of Naples
parts.note: remains looks like a verb meaning stays, but is a noun meaning ruins

explanation.surface: Someone stays close to Naples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as stays; it means archaeological ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruined Roman town buried by Vesuvius lies a short trip south-east of Naples.

clue.text: Turn up with mother cat

indicators.note: turn means the following word is turned round backwards

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother arrives with her cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar or mountain lion of the Americas is a big wild feline.

clue.text: Weapon company gets receiver in

indicators.note: gets, with in, means the company takes another piece inside it
in completes gets ... in, signalling one piece placed within another

parts.note: a firm is a business company
the ear receives sound, so it is a receiver

explanation.surface: An arms company takes delivery of a receiver, part of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun such as a rifle or pistol is a portable weapon.

clue.text: A circus performer?

parts.note: suggests a clown or acrobat, but refers to the novelty insect circus

explanation.walkthrough: A clown or acrobat comes to mind; the question mark points to a tiny insect act.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian novelty shows exhibited trained insects pulling tiny carts, known as flea circuses.

clue.text: With a degree, I leave this subject

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: leave means the letter I goes out of the word this

explanation.surface: A graduate says goodbye to a subject once qualified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave this' removes I from THIS, giving THS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics is a school subject; the British short form adds an S.

clue.text: Always on the go, remaining fresh and vital

indicators.note: on means one piece sits next to the other, joining them

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
green is the traffic-light colour meaning go

explanation.surface: Constantly busy, yet staying lively and youthful.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants keeping their leaves all year stay fresh, and the word extends to lasting popularity.
